Rearrange:

Three pairs of parametric equations are listed below:
$$\text{I}\quad \begin{cases}x=\sec t\\y=\tan t\end{cases}\quad \text{for }-\frac{\pi}{2}<t<\frac{\pi}{2}.$$
$$\text{II}\quad \begin{cases}x=\sqrt{1+t^2}\\y=t\end{cases}\quad \text{for }-\infty<t<\infty.$$

Also $x=\sqrt{1+t^2}>0$ and $y=t$ takes all real values, so II gives the full right branch.

For III:
$$\begin{align*}x^2-y^2&=t^2-(t^2-1)\\&=1\end{align*}$$

entries.description: Parametric Form

Parametric Form of an Equation
• Cartesian equations directly link x and y in one equation (like y = 2x + 1).
• In parametric equations, x and y are defined separately using a third variable (the parameter). Instead of y depending on x, both x and y depend on the parameter.
• Parametric equations are useful as they track multiple changing values at once. They have essential applications in future calculus topics such as projectile motion.
